title: Most polls now closed in GTA with election results coming soon

image.caption: The health club of the Allenway condo building in Ward 8 Eglinton-Lawrence is one of the 11 places where voting times have been extended. (Haydn Watters/CBC)

blocks.text: Who will lead Toronto and across the Greater Toronto Area? Watch CBC Toronto’s live election night special, starting at 7 p.m. ET on Oct. 26, for real-time results, expert analysis and on-the-ground reporting. We’re tracking the biggest mayoral battles and key Toronto city council races.

items: October 27Pool and politicsThe health club of the Allenway condo building in Ward 8 Eglinton-Lawrence is one of the 11 places where voting times have been extended. (Haydn Watters/CBC)Hello, I'm Haydn Watters and I'm a reporter with CBC Toronto’s Metro Morning radio show. Tonight, I’m going to be roaming the city speaking to new winners — those candidates who have never been elected to city council before. I don’t know exactly where I’m headed yet, so we're passing time at the health club of the Allenway condo building in Ward 8, Eglinton-Lawrence. It’s one of the 11 places where voting times have been extended. (This one was kept open until 8:10.)

Premier Ford 'ready to work' with tonight's winnersOlivia PierceyDid Ford hint at endorsing Olivia Chow for Mayor? Here’s what he said'The mayor and I have a phenomenal relationship,' said Premier Doug Ford Wednesday, alluding to a potential endorsement of Olivia Chow for mayor. CBC’s Shawn Jeffords breaks down what was said.Shortly after most polls closed, Ontario Premier Doug Ford made a post on X thanking candidates for putting themselves forward to serve the public. "Our government is ready to work with everyone who is elected tonight on the issues that matter most to Ontario families," Ford wrote. While Ford has not endorsed a candidate to be Toronto’s next mayor, his influence has loomed large in the municipal race. At one unrelated news conference in September, he appeared to all but endorse Chow, but he later walked it back, saying his statements were not an endorsement of the current mayor’s bid for re-election.

Caledon extends voting hours to 10 p.m.Isha BhargavaThe Town of Caledon has just announced it is extending voting hours until 10 p.m. at all voting locations due to what officials are calling "increased volume." We're checking what exactly that means and will report back.

Breaking down Pickering mayoral hopeful Lisa Robinson's controversial recordRochelle RaveendranControversial Pickering councillor Lisa Robinson is running against incumbent mayor Kevin Ashe. Since 2023, she’s been investigated nine times by the city's integrity commissioner for her conduct. (City of Pickering)Lisa Robinson is one of the most divisive figures on Pickering council. She’s running against incumbent mayor Kevin Ashe, with a long record of conduct complaints and pay suspensions behind her. The city's integrity commissioner has investigated Robinson's conduct nine times since 2023. She’s received multiple pay suspensions ranging from 30 to 90 days. The most recent investigation from June focused on comments Robinson made about residential schools. While the commissioner said they couldn’t ban what they called "residential school denialism," they recommended a 90-day pay suspension over comments the councillor made that were found to disrespect city staff. Robinson and Ashe have also repeatedly found themselves at odds. Back in January 2025, Ashe moved council meetings online, citing safety concerns he linked to Robinson’s supporters. That same month, CBC News reported that Ontario Provincial Police were investigating a criminal harassment complaint filed by Ashe on behalf of council. But police told CBC News the investigation ended in March 2026, with no evidence to support criminal charges.

When did Mississauga's race shift to a 3-way battle?Arrthy ThayaparanThis summer, polls and media coverage in Mississauga mainly centred on a Crombie versus Parrish mayoral race, said CBC panellist David Valentin. But once September hit, he said, Tedjo started making "big bold policy proposals" that led to a shift in support in the polls.The race's shift into a three-way battle was "super charged" after mayoral debates were held, Valentin said.

Crombie supporters confident she can win her old job backNav NanwaBonnie Crombie's supporters are starting to arrive at her election headquarters in Mississauga. Many have said they feel confident the city's former mayor will be elected to her old job once again. (Nav Nanwa/CBC)Hi everyone, I'm Nav Nanwa, host of CBC News Peel. I am coming to you from Bonnie Crombie's headquarters in Mississauga, right by Pearson airport. People are starting to file in, but it still feels a little early. Crombie is expected to arrive around 8 p.m. Regardless, people are enjoying some coffee, tea, Indian sweets like gulab jamun and periodically we're hearing soothing jazz music when the election feeds aren't on. The team members we've spoken to so far feel confident that tonight will be her night.

Most polls now closing in TorontoAlina SnisarenkoPolls across the city are now closing, and the vote counts will soon start trickling in. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)Good evening, I'm Alina Snisarenko, a digital reporter at CBC's Toronto newsroom. Polls across the city are now closing, and the vote counts will soon start trickling in. If you are in line at a polling station, stay there. You should still be able to cast your vote.There are also some polling stations that have extended their hours past the 8 p.m. closing time. The following locations have delayed closing times "due to disruptions earlier in the day," per a city news release: Ward 11, Wigwamen Terrace closes at 8:05 p.m.Ward 7, Driftwood Public School closes at 8:08 p.m. Ward 11, Casa 2 closes at 8:08 p.m.Ward 11 & 13, St. Joseph's College closes at 8:08 p.m. Ward 8, The Allenway closes at 8:10 p.m. Ward 11, Aura at College Park closes at 8:15 p.m.Ward 13, The Selby closes at 8:17 p.m.Ward 16, Valley Park Middle School closes at 8:18 p.m.Ward 2, Chartwell Scarlet Heights Retirement Residence closes at 8:20 p.m.Ward 5, Country Club Towers A closes at 8:20 p.m.Eligible voters can only cast their ballot in the ward they live in.You can catch the live count for the mayoral votes here.

October 26Supporters begin arriving at Carolyn Parrish’s election night partyJayden DillI'm Jayden Dill with CBC Peel, reporting from the Le Treport Wedding & Convention Centre, where current mayor Carolyn Parrish is holding her campaign party.The party hasn't started yet, but Parrish supporters are slowly trickling into the sounds of disco music and the smell of pork, roast beef and turkey sandwiches, among other hors d’oeuvres.Venue staff told us they're expecting hundreds of people, having laid out 200 chairs with plenty of standing room.Peter McCallion, son of the late Hazel McCallion, just arrived in his classic all-black suit and cowboy hat. Peter released a video supporting Parrish and blasting Crombie, saying his mother began regretting supporting former mayor Bonnie Crombie before she passed.

Brampton, Mississauga both saw high turnout for advance votingIsha BhargavaMore than 44,000 voters in Mississauga cast their ballots early, setting what the city calls "a new mark for advance voting turnout." It’s a 57 per cent increase from advance voting in the 2022 municipal election, the city said. Brampton boasted a similar increase. Nearly 25,000 Bramptonians cast their ballots during advance voting last week, according to the city — an estimated eight per cent increase compared to the previous municipal election. Historically, Peel Region has had one the lowest voter turnouts in an Ontario municipal election. In 2022, just under 22 per cent of Mississauga residents voted. That same year, the turnout in Brampton was also low with 24.56 per cent votes. Both cities were below the provincial average of 33 per cent.

When did we see a shift in Toronto’s mayoral polls?Arrthy ThayaparanPollsters have been covering the election campaign since January, said David Valentin, a CBC panellist and principal at Liaison Strategies. For a long time Bradford struggled to gain a foothold in the polls, he said on CBC Toronto's election special. But he got a boost in support after former mayor John Tory decided not to run, Chris Alexander withdrew from the race and he began debating Chow."It's always so hard going against an incumbent," Valentin said.
